_about: The toy library. build.py reads it for the "toys" setting. Each toy has its words (name, plural, label), a logo shape, and the starter text used when a club's toys differ from its preset's. "mix" is the shared text for those clubs; a preset can replace any part of it with its own "mix" block. Not a preset: the leading underscore keeps it out of the preset list.

yo-yo.name: yo-yo
yo-yo.label: Yo-Yo

card.title: Yo-Yo
card.text: Start with a responsive yo-yo. String to about 2 inches above your belly button, palm up, throw straight down.

links.title: YoYoTricks.com Trick Library
links.text: Video lessons from beginner to expert.

yo-yo.safety: Yo-yo: check your string before you throw. A worn string can snap and send a yo-yo flying. Keep looping and offstring play in open space.
yo-yo.equipment: Replace worn yo-yo strings, and stop if a yo-yo is cracked or damaged.

faq.q: Is it cheating to learn on an unresponsive yo-yo?
faq.a: No. A landed trick is a landed trick. Classic tricks are worth learning on a responsive yo-yo too, but there's no wrong way to play.

kendama.name: kendama
kendama.label: Kendama

card.title: Kendama
card.text: Hold the ken by the handle, let the tama hang still, and bend your knees as you pull it up.

level.label: Kendama
level.name: Kendama
level.text: Knees bent, eyes on the tama.

kendama.safety: Kendama: swings and juggles need room. Check around you first, and replace a frayed string before it snaps and sends the tama flying.
kendama.equipment: Replace frayed kendama strings, and stop if a tama is cracked.

faq.a: A little. Wooden tamas clack on the cups. We keep play in our space and keep it friendly for the venue.

spin-top.name: spin top
spin-top.label: Spin Top

card.title: Spin Tops
card.text: Wind the string tight from the tip up, then throw toward the floor and snap your hand back. A hard floor helps.

links.title: Skill Addicts: How to Spin a Top

spin-top.safety: Spin tops: throw toward the floor, never toward people, and only on a hard floor the venue says is okay. Mats protect floors from metal tips.
spin-top.equipment: Check a top's tip and string before you throw. A loose tip can fly off.

faq.q: What kind of floor do spin tops need?
faq.a: A hard, smooth floor like wood, tile, or concrete. Carpet and grass stop most tops. We meet where the floor works, and we use mats where the venue asks.

diabolo.name: diabolo
diabolo.label: Diabolo

card.title: Diabolo
card.text: Set it on the string, roll it to one side as you lift, then whip one stick in a steady rhythm to keep it spinning.

links.title: Diabolo on Wikipedia
links.text: Where it comes from and how it works.

community.title: International Jugglers' Association
community.text: Juggling and diabolo news and festivals.

diabolo.safety: Diabolo: tosses go up, so toss only where the ceiling is high, away from lights, windows, and people. Look up before every toss.
diabolo.equipment: Look up and around before a diabolo toss, and replace worn string before it snaps.

faq.q: How much space does diabolo need?
faq.a: More than you'd think. Tosses go up, so we play where the ceiling is high and there's room around each player, away from lights and windows.

juggling.name: juggling
juggling.label: Juggling

card.title: Juggling
card.text: Start with one ball, tossed hand to hand at eye level. Then two: throw the second when the first peaks.

juggling.safety: Juggling: clubs and rings need a clear circle around you. Practice props only at meetups: no knives, torches, or fire.
juggling.equipment: Juggle practice props only. No knives, torches, or fire at meetups.

faq.q: What do I need to start juggling?
faq.a: Three soft beanbags are all you need. Balls that don't bounce or roll away make practice much easier. We bring loaners.

flow-arts.name: flow arts
flow-arts.label: Flow Arts

card.title: Flow Arts
card.text: Poi, staff, and hoops are about smooth motion, not catches. Start slow with soft practice poi or a light hoop.

flow-arts.safety: Flow arts: poi, staffs, and hoops need a clear circle. Practice props only at meetups: no fire.
flow-arts.equipment: Spin practice props only. Fire spinning needs its own space, safety gear, and the venue's permission.

faq.a: Not to our meetups. Fire spinning needs its own space, safety gear, and the venue's permission. Bring practice props instead.

about: {name} is a {toy} community for {area}. We meet up to learn tricks, trade tips, and hang out with people who love to practice. {welcome}.
Never tried it? Working on something hard? This is your crew. {loaners} Someone will always help you land your first trick.

pillars.title: Learn
pillars.text: New to it? Someone will show you your first trick. Stuck on a hard one? Someone's done it.

pillars.title: Play
pillars.text: Jam sessions, challenges, and games anyone can join. No experience needed.

pillars.title: Progress
pillars.text: Work through the trick list with people who've been there. Compete if you want to, or never. Up to you.

pillars.title: Share
pillars.text: Try other people's gear, swap tips, and learn how to care for your {toys}.

program.meetup_blurb: A free, drop-in {toy} meetup. Beginners welcome, loaners available.
program.donate_text: Meetups are free, always. Donations cover loaner {toys}, spare parts, and venue costs.

loaners.yes: We bring loaner {toys} to every meetup, so you don't need to bring anything.
loaners.no: Bring your {toys} if you have them. Don't have any? Email us and we'll try to have a spare.

learn.title: Learn the Basics
learn.intro: Every trick starts the same way: one small move, practiced until it clicks. Pick a toy and start here, then come to a meetup and we'll help in person.
learn.levels_intro: A starter list for each toy. Skip around. Every landed trick counts.
learn.outro: Learning is faster in person. Bring your questions to the next meetup.

faq.a: {name} is a {toy} club for {area}. We bring together {players} {ages}, from total beginners to experienced players. {welcome}.
{toy_list}. Bring what you love, or try something new with a loaner.
Not at all. Most people come to hang out, learn tricks, and have fun. Competing is up to you.

faq.q: When and where do you meet?
faq.a: {meetup}. We meet at {venue}, {address}. Come and go anytime during the meetup.
No. Just show up. If a meetup is ever cancelled, we post it on this site and our social media as early as we can.
Nothing. {loaners} Wear comfortable clothes you can move in.
Yes! All ages are welcome. Younger kids should come with a parent or guardian, especially the first time.

faq.q: Do I need to know any tricks?
faq.a: No. Total beginners are just as welcome as experienced players. We'll help you with your first trick.
Nothing, yet. Try the loaners at a meetup, then ask our members. They'll help you pick something for your budget.

faq.q: How do I become a member?
faq.a: Just come to a meetup. There's no sign-up. If you show up, you're part of the club.
Yes, please. Email {email} or talk to us at a meetup. We always need help setting up, greeting newcomers, and running activities.

faq.q: Can my organization partner with the club?
faq.a: Yes. We're open to venue partnerships, demos, workshops, and sponsorships. Email {email} with your idea.

points: Kids are welcome. Younger kids need a parent or guardian with them. A parent or guardian is responsible for their own child at every meetup.
Club volunteers never take kids anywhere away from the group or the meetup space.
Give everyone room. Look around before a big trick, and check your gear before you play.

conduct.intro: {name} is built on the idea that {toys} should be fun and welcoming for everyone. That only works if people treat each other well. This code sets out what we expect from everyone in our community.
expected: Be respectful. Treat everyone with dignity, whatever their age, skill level, race, ethnicity, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, religion, or background.
Be welcoming, especially to beginners and younger players. Everyone was new once.
Keep feedback encouraging. If someone asks for tips, help. Skip the harsh criticism.
Mind the space. Keep the venue clean, watch your reach, and look out for kids.
Respect decisions. Raise disagreements with organizers calmly and privately.
equipment_first: Ask before you borrow someone's gear. Hand it back the way you got it.
Look before you play. Big tricks and tosses need open space.
